title: Rounding of a Late Payment Fee Correction, by Savings Relationship
content:
How the figure obtained for a late payment fee correction on a card under Personal Credit Cards is rounded is read from the cardholder's holdings under Savings & Money Market Accounts.

| What the savings records show | How the figure is rounded |
|---|---|
| An active savings account whose balance is at least 25000.00 USD, and at least 1 savings deposit posted to the cardholder's savings accounts in the last three months | rounded half-up to the nearest whole dollar |
| An active savings account whose balance is below 25000.00 USD, and at least 1 savings deposit posted to the cardholder's savings accounts in the last three months | reduced to the whole dollar below it |
| Neither of those | rounded half-up to the cent |

**Both parts of each condition.** Each of the first two rows requires an active savings account of the stated balance and the savings deposit count in the stated window together. A cardholder holding an active savings account of 31000.00 USD with no savings deposit in the last three months falls in the third row; so does a cardholder with three savings deposits in the last three months but no active savings account.

**Worked on hypothetical figures.** A figure of 14.62 becomes 15.00 USD under the first convention, 14.00 USD under the second and 14.62 USD under the third. A figure of 12.50 becomes 13.00 USD under the first, 12.00 USD under the second and 12.50 USD under the third. A balance of exactly 25000.00 USD belongs to the first row, since the test is at least that amount, and a balance of 24999.00 USD to the second.
